record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; the report, notebooks, and result files are listed but their contents are not included.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes applying difference-of-means steering vectors to concepts, but reports no test of refusal or of the refusal-specific claim versions.
record.gate_note: The README reports concept-steering results, not refusal rates or refusal-direction interventions. It does not name the models or provide the report's underlying tables. Its reported results are recorded as findings about general concept steering, not as tests of V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The project uses raw difference-of-means steering directions for general concepts, not refusal, and compares direction sources. It reports no refusal rates and no ablation or induction of refusal, so no version is tested. It could arguably be T6, since it relies on diff-of-means steering generally rather than on the refusal-direction finding.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Logit-lens accuracy per layer predicts steerability, while the saturated probe cannot. The anchor paper's ranking depends partly on unequal doses. Layer and dose matter more than direction source, and a random direction wins on one concept.
record.recipe_differences: Uses raw difference-of-means additions for concept steering, but the README does not specify harmful-versus-harmless instructions or refusal, and reports no refusal ablation or induction. The README calls the project a reproduction of an unnamed anchor paper.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports effects associated with dose and layer; at layer 10, the direction-source comparison is described, and a random direction wins for one concept.

fits_no_version.finding: The raw difference-of-means vector norm ranges from 0.5 to 58 across concepts and layers. At an equal side-effect budget, the anchor paper's steerability ranking mostly survives, with one adjacent swap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unnormalized diff-of-means steering compares concepts at unequal doses; dose partly drives the reported steerability rankings.

fits_no_version.finding: At layer 10, diff-of-means, probe-weight and SAE decoder-row directions land within 0.03 of each other. On one concept, a same-norm random direction beats all three.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For concept steering, layer and dose matter more than how the direction is derived.

fits_no_version.finding: Logit-lens accuracy per layer predicts concept steerability. A trained probe saturates at 1.00 in all layers for two of six concept families.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear readability of a concept does not imply steerability; probe accuracy saturates.

record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other README findings about logit-lens accuracy and trained-probe saturation concern predicting concept steerability, not the refusal-direction claim.
